sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the object of 'call out to ___' from verse 3. No earlier card told this line, and 'heaven' or 'the elders' fit just as well. It is guessing the wording of a line, not reasoning.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. / The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The text gives conditions ('if you accept... and hide...', 'if you incline...'). Card 3 turns them into commands ('He tells the son to keep his commandments hidden inside'), which drops the 'if'. Cards 4, 5 and 6 do the same ('The son is told to', 'tells the son just how hard to look', 'He says to search').

Story card 12 already says the son 'will discern righteousness and justice and equity'. The True statement on card 13 ('able to tell which paths are good') just restates that, so the card before gives away the answer.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it. / No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The story card has no content from verse 18. It only says 'very serious' and 'Lean in, friend', so it doesn't tell part of the passage.
sonnet.rule: Every story card tells part of the passage.

sonnet.problem: 'Very serious about where her house leads' hints at something grim. That rules out the wrong answers on card 8 ('Down to the sea', 'Down to Egypt') before the baker chooses.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: 'elders' was already a wrong answer on stop 1 card 4 ('the elders') and card 7 ('A seat among the elders'). 'kings' repeats 'king' from card 9 and returns on card 13 ('rule over the land as kings'). 'Silver' (right answer on stop 1 card 6) comes back as a wrong answer on card 7.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: Papa Dorin says he himself watches a movie and yells at the screen. Things outside his bakery are supposed to come up as things people do, not as his own habits.
sonnet.rule: Things outside his bakery, like a phone or a car, come up as things people do: "You know when your phone…"

sonnet.problem: 'In the end' adds a time the verse doesn't give. Proverbs 2:22 says only that the wicked 'will be cut off from the land'.
sonnet.rule: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
